title: UK to draft in military aircraft to fight wildfires, Burnham says
description: RAF Chinook crews have already helped respond, external to wildfires in Cyprus.In addition to military aircraft, the government said it would also spe
body: RAF Chinook crews have already helped respond, external to wildfires in Cyprus.In addition to military aircraft, the government said it would also spend £45m on wildfire-specific personal protective equipment for firefighters on the ground.It is lighter than current firefighting equipment which is designed for fires in buildings and not meant to be worn for a long time, the government added.Ministers are also pledging a £25m scheme from April 2027 to April 2029 to restore dried-out peatlands in England so they are natural firebreaks, and financial support for farmers to fireproof their land such as by digging ponds."The government will also look at tougher local restrictions or product bans to stop people starting fires when the risk is high," a briefing ahead of the summit said, following a temporary ban on disposable BBQs.Burnham will meet fire chiefs, local leaders and experts from tech companies at the summit."I stood in Stourbridge and watched families lose everything," he said on Thursday, recounting the night of a wildfire that destroyed 19 homes in the West Midlands in August."I will never forget it. Our firefighters were heroes that day, but heroes shouldn't have to fight with one hand tied behind their backs."Earlier this month, MPs on the Environment, Food and Rural Affairs Committee said there were weaknesses in the UK's wildfire preparedness, including access to aerial firefighting resources, securing water supplies during major incidents and coordinating resources at a national level.

schema.headline: UK to draft in military aircraft to fight wildfires, Burnham says

title: Woman charged after police officer injured in Nottingham shooting
description: A 27-year-old woman has been charged after a police officer was shot in Nottingham city centre.Nottinghamshire Police said the officer was shot in the
body: A 27-year-old woman has been charged after a police officer was shot in Nottingham city centre.Nottinghamshire Police said the officer was shot in the foot after he approached a man and a woman at a bus stop in Angel Row shortly before 04:50 BST on Sunday.The male officer remains in hospital receiving treatment, the force added.Aisha Zaman, of Collison Street, Hyson Green, has been charged with possession of a prohibited firearm and possession of that firearm with intent to commit an indictable offence.Police said the charge came after "consultation with the Crown Prosecution Service".Zaman has been remanded into custody and will appear before Nottingham Magistrates' Court on Friday, police added.Several other people have been arrested in connection with the incident, including two men, 24 and 30, and two women, 25 and 21, who have been arrested on suspicion of assisting an offender.A 35-year-old man and a 33-year-old woman have also been arrested on suspicion of possession of a firearm with intent to endanger life and assisting an offender. Both remain in police custody.Det Ch Supt Rich Bull, who is leading the investigation, said the "outpouring of support" for the officer had been "greatly appreciated". "We would just like to take this moment to thank the public", he added."We continue to support him as he undergoes further treatment in hospital and keeping him and his family fully informed of the developments in this investigation."He said officers were "still following a number of lines of inquiry", and anyone with information has been asked to contact the force.

schema.headline: Woman charged after police officer injured in Nottingham shooting

title: Russell Brand accuser said alleged rape 'really hurt', court hears
description: Image source, Getty ImagesBySima KotechaSenior UK correspondent at Southwark Crown Court   and Helen BushbyCulture reporterUpdated 6 hours agoWarning
body: Image source, Getty ImagesBySima KotechaSenior UK correspondent at Southwark Crown Court   and Helen BushbyCulture reporterUpdated 6 hours agoWarning - this report contains graphic contentThe friend of a woman claiming to have been raped by Russell Brand told a jury the complainant had told her after the alleged attack that it had "really, really hurt".The witness who spoke via video link at his trial said she had attended the Hammersmith Apollo theatre in London with the alleged victim in 2009, where they had been invited to the defendant's dressing room after his comedy show.Statements from the woman's parents were also heard in court, saying their daughter had told them about the alleged attack, and that she had been "very worried about HIV".Brand, 51, has pleaded not guilty to all seven charges in the trial - three counts of rape, three charges of sexual assault and one of indecent assault.The allegations span a 10-year period from 1999 to 2009 and involve six female complainants.The witness said the woman had told her she had visited Brand's house in London soon after meeting at the theatre, and that he then sent a car to collect the woman, which took her to his place in Hampstead.She said when they spoke about it "quite soon after",  she said she "was just crying - really upset".The witness said Brand had forced her into having anal sex at the end of an encounter that started off consensually."He was quite aggressive," she said her friend had told her."He forcibly put it in my bum and "it really really hurt".The witness says she remembers specifically asking the complainant if she had said no to Brand when the alleged attack started.Russell Brand on TrialYou can follow the trial day by day on the BBC podcast Russell Brand on Trial - available on BBC Sounds, YouTube, iPlayer, or wherever you get your BBC podcastsShe said the woman replied "lots of times"."She told me that she was in a lot of pain" and that "she couldn't sit down".Another friend of the same complainant also gave evidence to the court.From the witness box, she told the jury her friend had told her that she had told him to stop during the alleged rape.She said her friend had said the worst moment had been after the act, and "she said that Brand told her she'd been dirty and had to clean up her mess"."She said he was quite cold and keen to get her gone".The witness said she had given her friend advice after she had confided in her. "I told her that she should go and get checked out because she had anal tears and a lot of discomfort and to seek guidance from her parents and to go to the police. "She just wasn't sure - it was all a bit chaotic in her head. She felt like it wasn't worth it."She told jurors: "She didn't think she would be believed, and she didn't think it would be worth it to go."She kind of put it behind her."Parents' statementsStatements from the alleged rape victim's parents said their daughter stayed with them for about two months after the alleged incident with Brand. Her mother's statement said: "I just remember her saying 'he raped me'."She was very worried about HIV," she said, adding that her daughter had started talking about it during a car journey."She said she went to his place, went to see him, as she had always admired him."Her father recalled their daughter being "very upset and very unwell", during the stay, that that she was "upset by something that had happened to her."The father said in his statement that his daughter told him: "They were having sex, she asked him to stop, she kept saying she had been assaulted."I turned to her in the car and asked if she asked him to stop, and she said 'no' several times."I said 'you have been raped, that's rape'."He said his daughter got a sexual health check, and he said he had only recently learned his daughter is accusing Brand of anal rape.Former boyfriend's statementThe woman's former boyfriend also gave evidence, telling the court she was "very upset" whenever she talked about her encounter with Brand, and that "she characterised it as an assault... she called it rape". Brand's barrister Ian Winter KC cross-examined the woman's former boyfriend and read parts of the statement he gave in June 2025, in which he said the woman had "come round" to having anal sex.When asked if he had said that, the witness replied: "Yes."The witness added the woman had "surrendered to the idea". "If I was being attacked, you either fight back or surrendered, it doesn't negate the attack," he added. Judge Mr Justice Bennathan sent the jury away until Monday morning, at the end of Thursday's evidence.He told the jurors that "we aim to finish the prosecution case on Monday", adding the defence case would not begin before Tuesday morning.

schema.headline: Russell Brand accuser said alleged rape 'really hurt', court hears

title: Raye wins the Mercury Prize with This Music May Contain Hope
description: Raye has won the 2026 Mercury Prize for her show-stopping second album This Music May Contain Hope.A pop record sprinkled with golden age Hollywood gl
body: Raye has won the 2026 Mercury Prize for her show-stopping second album This Music May Contain Hope.A pop record sprinkled with golden age Hollywood glamour, it beat the likes of Sir Paul McCartney, Olivia Dean and Jade to scoop the £25,000 prize."I couldn't tell you how grateful I am to be holding this," said Raye, clutching her trophy at Newcastle's Utilita Arena. "I'm shaking, I'm jet-lagged, I'm tired. It's all blurry."It is the first time a pop album has won the coveted prize - which recognises the best British or Irish album of the last 12 months - since M People's Elegant Slumming in 1994.Speaking to the BBC afterwards, Raye said she'd "poured everything I had" into the record, which features the global hit song Where Is My Husband?"I made this album not focusing on commercial [success], not focusing on making things cookie-cutter," said the 28-year-old."Some of these songs are seven minutes. They're indulgent. They're maximalist."Across 17 tracks and 73 minutes, the record tells a cinematic story about a relationship that ends in tears on the rainy streets of Paris, then follows our plucky heroine as she dusts off the debris and emerges stronger and more resilient.Along the way, it features both of her grandparents, the soul legend Al Green, four separate orchestras and more than 100 musicians.But the album almost never happened. Two years ago this week, the singer's car was stolen, along with all of her songwriting notebooks and demos.Although they were eventually recovered, it delayed work on This Music May Contain Hope by almost a year.Looking back, she was philosophical about the delay."I was distraught. I was very worried, but you know, it all turned out great. "Every little slip, every little accident, every little thing, it creates the path that you take. "And it's easy to spend time wishing things were the other way. But right now, I certainly do not."Established in 1992, the Mercury Prize was envisaged as an antidote to the commercially-focused Brit Awards, recognising albums that moved music forwards, without recourse to fashion or trends.Of the last 35 winners, 20 have been debut albums - from artists including Arctic Monkeys, Suede and Franz Ferdinand.Many people have mistakenly assumed it is a prize for first albums - but this year's shortlist included only two: Dove Ellis's heartfelt and delicate Blizzard, and Jade's That's Showbiz, Baby. In the run-up to this year's ceremony, Olivia Dean had been the bookmakers' favourite for her second album, The Art of Loving.An easy-going, soulful collection of love songs, it had already been named album of the year at the Brit Awards and the Mobos, and is widely expected to earn the singer a Grammy nomination in the same category next month.Speaking backstage, the singer said she was overwhelmed by the success."I don't think I've processed it yet, to be honest," she said. "I feel like I'm still in this crazy whirlwind of it all."And maybe, when I take a break over Christmas, I'll reflect on the sofa."Other nominees included the rapper Kojey Radical, Geordie jazz act Knats, and former Little Mix star Jade - who was the first ever X Factor winner to receive a Mercury nomination.The shortlist also included the charity compilation album Help (2), recorded in aid of Warchild, which featured new music and cover versions by artists such as Olivia Rodrigo, Damon Albarn, Depeche Mode and The Last Dinner Party.The tracklist also included nine former Mercury Prize winners: Arctic Monkeys, Young Fathers, Wolf Alice, Pulp, Sampha, Portishead's Beth Gibbons, Arlo Parks, English Teacher and Ezra Collective.Last year, the prize was won by Newcastle singer-songwriter Sam Fender, who donated his £25,000 winnings to grassroots music venues, helping to support up-and-coming songwriters around the UK.

schema.headline: Raye wins the Mercury Prize with This Music May Contain Hope

title: Race to update services' computer systems after cyber-security flaw found
description: Organisations and businesses are still scrambling to update their systems after cyber-security flaws were revealed in a widely-used programming langua
body: Organisations and businesses are still scrambling to update their systems after cyber-security flaws were revealed in a widely-used programming language, PHP.Websites around the world were taken offline on Wednesday and Thursday after the developers of PHP said "critical vulnerabilities" were found in the back-end language, used in web development for decades.Researchers warned the "severe" flaws could expose millions of sites using it to potential hacks if left unpatched - and the UK government was among those to take some sites offline as a precaution.There have been no successful attacks reported so far, but experts say any impact may take time - even months - to become fully apparent.Downing Street said on Thursday "some" limited government services "may be offline" while security work was being carried out."The information I have is that 32 Government services are unavailable and four are partially unavailable," tech minister Baroness Lloyd of Effra told the House of Lords.She attributed this to having "largely resulted from precautionary measures taken to protect systems while security updates and mitigations are applied".The government did not specify which services were taken offline - but it said no large UK public-facing critical services had been affected.A spokesperson said work had already taken place across government to "identify and fix potential exposures to our systems and our experts are continuing to work closely with both OpenAI and international partners on this issue"."But this does not mean they were hacked, and work continues to resolve any issues," they added.Olly Whitehouse, chief technology officer of the National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC), called the event "unprecedented"."It will be universally felt, I suspect," he told BBC Radio 4's World At One.But he said there were "no indications" of any successful breaches by hackers.He said the NCSC was "starting to see positive confirmation" that advice sent to those affected, external had been received and was being acted on.Cyber-security lecturer Rory Hopcraft told the BBC the government needed to make sure that its own infrastructure was up-to-date."Hacking has been around for many years," he said."The government are the ones who set the rules for other organisations... they just need to effectively be practising what they're preaching at this point."Dean Presley, who has a garage in Chepstow, South Wales, told BBC Your Voice he had been unable to properly process MOTs online.He said his computer system had been down since Wednesday morning, and while he has experienced outages before, they have not lasted this long."MOTs can be conducted and they're legal but none of the paperwork and certificates can be printed and they're not on the system," Dean said.He said this has forced him to write everything on paper documents, leading to delays for customers.PHP stands for PHP: Hypertext Preprocessor.It's a programming language which runs on a web server, behind the scenes of a website, and effectively lets you see the sites you visit.When you go to a site, PHP is the code which collects data and effectively turns it into a page you can read.It was developed in the early 1990s to help serve dynamic web pages and applications, but still powers lots of platforms today. PHP has been used across a wide range of platforms including Wikipedia, online shops and WordPress – the system behind many websites - as well as to write tools to build web apps, with Laravel, Symfony and Drupal among popular PHP frameworks.According to cyber-security firm Wiz, external, which helped uncover the critical PHP vulnerabilities surfaced this week, PHP powers 70% of the world's websites. And it said the flaws - now coined "php2shell" - were inherent in the language itself, affecting many past versions of it.The PHP Foundation, the non-profit which maintains the programming language, warned this meant that, under the right conditions, an unauthenticated attacker would be able to remotely execute code on servers running PHP.Some large organisations said they had seen a high volume of attempts to breach their systems.Matthew Prince, the boss of internet infrastructure firm Cloudflare, wrote on X, external on Thursday that the company saw "thousands" of attempts to exploit the PHP vulnerabilities across its network in the 10 hours before it was publicly announced."That jumped to tens of thousands in the 45 minutes post announcement, hundreds of thousands within two hours, and millions now," he added.Amazon also says it saw hackers attempt to exploit the flaws, but its websites were operating as normal.While the impact of the PHP flaw remains to be seen, disruption continued for businesses and organisations after many sites were taken down on Wednesday.The website of a Dutch agency specialising in cyber-security, Finland's government and parts of Wikipedia, taken temporarily offline, had returned to business as usual by Thursday.But a number of sites appeared to have been taken offline on Thursday, as operators rushed to check if PHP might be running within their systems or if any patches were required.In France, telecommunications company Orange also said, external it had suspended access to certain services globally while it deployed security fixes.According to some cyber-security researchers using scans to check servers at risk of the PHP vulnerability, the rate of organisations implementing patches - but not as quickly as might be hoped globally."The window to respond has shrunk dramatically," said Matt Hull, VP of cyber intelligence and response at global cyber security company NCC Group."A few years ago, attackers might have taken weeks to exploit a vulnerability. Now, it can be days or hours."Hull also highlighted the extent of the task facing developers and engineers working to deal with the issue."Several days into this incident, security professionals might already be dealing with significant burnout," he said, urging a need to "make time to rest, share the workload and look after each other"."Resilience depends on people as much as technology."

schema.headline: Race to update services' computer systems after cyber-security flaw found

title: Bruno Fernandes has home burgled while in Italy with Man Utd
description: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes had his home burgled on Wednesday while he was in Italy for his club's Champions League game against Como.It
body: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes had his home burgled on Wednesday while he was in Italy for his club's Champions League game against Como.It is understood Fernandes' family were not in the house in Cheshire when it was broken into and that the intruders were inside for less than five minutes before police arrived.United are understood to be supporting the 32-year-old following the break-in.BBC Sport has contacted Cheshire Police about the incident.He is the latest player to have his family home burgled while playing for his team.Manchester City player Ruben Dias and former girlfriend Maya Jama also had their Cheshire home burgled in similar circumstances to Fernandes.Dias was at City's Champions League game against Galatasaray when his home was targeted in January.Previous victims in the same area include footballers Jack Grealish, Raheem Sterling and Riyad Mahrez.Portugal midfielder Fernandes has been with Manchester United since joining from Sporting in January 2020.United were beaten 4-1 by Como and, following the match, Fernandes criticised his manager Michael Carrick's tactics.However, he will remain as the club's captain and will not be disciplined for his comments.

schema.headline: Bruno Fernandes has home burgled while in Italy with Man Utd

title: How Arab parties could hold critical balance of power in Israeli election
description: Image caption, Students in Nazareth are handing out leaflets encouraging Arab Israelis to vote in next week's electionByYolande KnellMiddle East corre
body: Image caption, Students in Nazareth are handing out leaflets encouraging Arab Israelis to vote in next week's electionByYolande KnellMiddle East correspondentReporting fromNazarethAt rush hour in Nazareth, the largest Arab-majority city in Israel, students are handing out leaflets by the roadside urging motorists to vote in next week's closely fought, general election. Polls indicate that Arab parties could be left holding a critical balance of power.Disaffection has often driven down past turnout among Arab Israelis - who account for about a fifth of the population and often describe themselves as Palestinian citizens of Israel. But this election, there is a strong push to get rid of the most right-wing governing coalition in the country's history - an alliance between veteran Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and far-right and ultra-Orthodox parties."I see it as our duty to bring down this extremist government. They treat us as second-class," says Arkan Badran, 23, who is with the students giving out flyers. "I call on all young men and women to vote for Arab lists, which represent us, because this is our future."Image caption, All but one of the leading Jewish parties have ruled out forming a coalition government with Arab partiesMost opinion polls indicate that neither Netanyahu and his partners nor the main "Change Bloc", led by centre-right former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, has a clear path to a parliamentary majority.If they are right, after the election anti-Netanyahu parties wanting to form a governing coalition would either have to go back on pledges not to work with the prime minister or make a deal with Arab-majority lists.A major sticking point is that Eisenkot has so far ruled out forming a government with Arab parties, citing a lack of shared values.Israel's politics and society have been changed by the deadly, unprecedented Hamas-led assault on the country on 7 October 2023, and subsequent war in Gaza. There is increased mistrust of and hostility towards the country's Arab minority.Image caption, Salman Mousa accuses ministers of "systematic discrimination and incitement" against Arab Israelis"After October 7, we were treated as enemies of this country," says Suha Salman Mousa of the Mossawa Centre in Nazareth, which advocates for equal rights for Arab citizens. "There was shrinking space for freedom of speech. There were major arrests, there was also firing of people from their workplaces because they put something on social media or they went out against the war on Gaza."Salman Mousa accuses ministers of "systematic discrimination and incitement" against Arab Israelis. Civil society groups say they have disproportionately cut budgets for Arab communities. The government says reductions are needed to fund wartime defence and security spending.There have also been politicised campaigns against Arab physicians working in Israeli hospitals and racially motivated attacks on Arab bus drivers by Jewish Israelis.Some electioneering has sought to capitalise by deepening social divisions. The far-right Finance Minister, Bezalel Smotrich, has vowed to "Judaise" parts of the northern Galilee and southern Negev regions where most Arabs live, likening this to expanding settlements in the occupied West Bank.The majority of Arab Israelis are descendants of Palestinians who remained within what became Israel during the war that surrounded the creation of the state in 1948, when hundreds of thousands were forced from or fled their homes. Israel's current government often frames them as a threat to the state's Jewish identity.  Recently, the prime minister has claimed that his rivals plan to team up with Arabs and form a "dangerous government".To make this point, his campaign has put up billboards, including one at a road junction at the main entrance to Nazareth. They suggest a choice between: "Right or Palestine" - with pictures of main opposition figures, including right-wingers, depicted as representing the latter not the former. The Netanyahu campaign has also used AI-generated videos to present his opponents embracing Arab leaders.Image caption, Radio Nas anchor Mohammed Magadli says Benjamin Netanyahu is trying to delegitimise Arab partiesAt Radio Nas, a popular Arabic-language station in Nazareth, I meet news anchor Mohammed Magadli, who is also an analyst for Israel's Channel 12. His father, Raleb Magadli, served as Israel's first Muslim minister between 2007 and 2009, representing the Labour party. I ask the younger Magadli what he makes of Change Bloc leaders refusing to join forces with Arab parties."In a word it's racism. But if we're trying to explain why, it's because of the political interests of Benjamin Netanyahu," he says. "He's trying all the time to pull the legitimacy of the Arab parties - because they're Arab, because they're Palestinian. This is affecting the majority of the Jewish parties in Israel."Polls this week have suggested that both Eisenkot's bloc and Netanyahu's religious-nationalist bloc could each win around 50 seats of the 120 in Israel's parliament while 13 or 14 seats in total could go to Arab-majority groupings. These are the Joint Arab List, a coalition of Hadash, Balad and Taal, and the smaller United Arab List, an Islamist party headed by politician Mansour Abbas.Image caption, United Arab List leader Mansour Abbas wants Arab parties to reach a "position of influence"While Abbas's party was originally created as part of the Islamic Movement in Israel - which has socially conservative values - he has become known for joining with Jewish partners. He prioritises solving the problems of Arab Israelis and speaks relatively little of Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza.Abbas has had a taste of power. In 2021, he became a minister in a previous, short-lived Israeli government led by Naftali Bennett - now a right-wing member of Eisenkot's bloc. For this election, he has taken the surprise step of giving the number two position on his slate to a Jewish former police official and centrist member of parliament, Yoav Segalovitz. Abbas believes Eisenkot and others will be more open to an alliance with his party after the election and insists he wants to join the next government."We've reached the conclusion that parliamentary representation is not enough to serve Arab society. We decided to take responsibility, to become part of the solution to our problems and to offer hope to both Arabs and Jews," he tells me. "That's why our approach has been driven by a desire to reach a position of influence, not merely representation."Image source, ReutersImage caption, The Joint List talks of providing an electoral "safety net" to those who could replace Netanyahu's governmentMeanwhile, the Joint List - which is made up of secular parties and advocates for equal rights for Arab Israelis, an end to Israeli military occupation of Palestinian territories, and a two-state solution to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict - aims to wield a position of influence within the opposition. It talks of providing an electoral "safety net" to those who could replace the Netanyahu government, in return for support on important policies.A main issue in this election for Arab Israelis is rampant gang crime. In September, a poll by the Israel Democracy Institute think tank found that this was the most important factor for 53.5% of Arab citizens when deciding which party to vote for. Murders within the community reached a record high of 252 last year – about five times higher than the number of Jewish Israelis who were killed, according to the Abraham Initiatives, a Jewish-Arab organisation that promotes coexistence.Image caption, Arab Israelis accuse the government of inaction on the issue of gang crimeIn Jaffa, a mixed Arab-Jewish neighbourhood which is now joined to Tel Aviv, Ziad Samouni shows me where his son, Hussein, was shot dead by two gunmen on a motorcycle near his home last November. No arrests have been made in his case. With a low percentage of cases solved, Arab-Israelis accuse the government of inaction."It seems they're interested in making sure we reach a situation where the killer is never caught, allowing Arabs in Arab society to keep killing one another," says Samouni, who is now part of a support group, Israeli-Palestinian Bereaved Families for Peace.The Israeli police told the BBC its investigation into Hussein's murder remained active, adding that it took "every case of violence and crime with the utmost seriousness.""As a father who's lost a son, of course, I want this bloodshed to end," Samouni tells me. "I wish every Arab citizen who believes there needs to be a change sees that this is a time to go to vote."Image source, Ziad SamouniImage caption, Ziad Samouni's son Hussein (2nd L) was shot dead last November but no arrests have been made This month, Israel's Supreme Court overruled a decision by the Central Elections Committee to disqualify the United Arab List and the Joint List as well as two of their members.The committee, which is dominated by the governing coalition, argued that they broke a law banning candidates who deny the existence of Israel as a Jewish state. The parties and their representatives strongly denied it.With just days to go before voting, back in Nazareth, some motorists display flags for their preferred party on their cars.The stakes are high in this election: Arab citizens could yet decide who wields power in Israel, and they also see this vote as key to their own future in the country.

schema.headline: How Arab parties could hold critical balance of power in Israeli election

title: Lockerbie bombing accused Abu Agila Mas'ud al-Marimi loses bid to have case thrown out
description: She referred to a longstanding American legal doctrine, which stipulates that a court's right to hold a trial is not impaired if the suspect has been
body: She referred to a longstanding American legal doctrine, which stipulates that a court's right to hold a trial is not impaired if the suspect has been the subject of a forceful abduction."This rule rests on the principle that due process of law is satisfied when one present in court is convicted of a crime after a fair trial and in accordance with constitutional procedural safeguards," said the judge."Put differently, there's nothing in the Constitution that requires a court to permit a guilty person rightfully convicted to escape justice because he was brought to trial against his will."In her ruling, the judge said there were two exceptions to that doctrine.One would apply if Marimi had been brought before the court through the US government's "deliberate, unnecessary and unreasonable invasion" of his constitutional rights.For that exception to be triggered, the challenged conduct had to be carried out by, or at the direction of, US officials.The judge said Marimi's allegations "at best suggest that US government officials exerted pressure on Libyan officials to facilitate a rendition, not that US government officials directed or controlled the challenged conduct."The second exception to the doctrine would apply if the US government had violated an extradition agreement which was the only way a suspect could be transferred between the two countries.The judge said the US government had invoked two conventions to secure Marimi's appearance in a US court."Neither the Montreal Convention nor the Terrorists Bombing Convention provides that it is the only way by which one country may gain custody of a national of another country for the purposes of prosecution," she said."Accordingly, Libya was free to transfer Mr Al-Marimi to the United States using any method it chose."The defence and prosecution have fought a series of legal battles in the approach to Marimi's trial, which is now scheduled to get underway on 19 January after three postponements.In another ruling, the judge rejected a defence motion to suppress a confession alleged to have been made by Marimi when he was in custody in Libya in 2012.According to the FBI, Marimi admitted building the bomb which destroyed Pan Am 103 in an operation carried out by the Libyan intelligence service.Marimi has claimed the confession was false and was made under duress.The only previous criminal trial related to the Lockerbie bombing took place between May 2000 and January 2001, when three Scottish judges convicted Libyan intelligence agent Abdulbasset al-Megrahi of playing a key role in the plot.Megrahi was jailed for life but released on compassionate grounds by the Scottish government in 2009 after he was diagnosed with terminal cancer. He died three years later at home in Tripoli.

schema.headline: Lockerbie bombing accused Abu Agila Mas'ud al-Marimi loses bid to have case thrown out

title: United States Grand Prix: Max Verstappen says Austin track bumps 'unacceptable' and 'out of control'
description: The track is built on former marshland and that has made it difficult for organisers to keep it in good condition, but the four-time champion rejected
body: The track is built on former marshland and that has made it difficult for organisers to keep it in good condition, but the four-time champion rejected that as a reason not to try to solve the issue."You can use the excuse that the soil is the problem but then you should have known that and you need to make sure that you reinforce it more," Verstappen said."Last year, for example, you pull around 5-6G in a corner, but I had some impacts, vertical load, which was over 9G on my spine, which I can tell you is really not fun, and especially the older you get, you think about that more and more."Verstappen said the problem was likely to be exacerbated this year because although the cars from 2022-25 had lower ride-heights overall, the way the cars are run under the latest regulations means they are running lower in corners than last season.That's because of the switch between having the front and rear wings open in drag-reduction mode on the straights and closing in corners means the cars drop down towards the ground when they brake."You bottom out way harder, because when the wings close and the ride-height comes down, under braking is actually a very stressful moment, and I know around here in some places, it's very bumpy under braking," he said."Especially when it's like these kind of awkward bumps, not just bumps from the track getting older, but the surface underneath the soil just moving up and down, sometimes (it's) very hard to expect, or if you're like a tiny bit offline, you don't know what is there, because no-one really drives here sometimes."I can tell you from the checks that I've done from my spine, the bottom end doesn't look that great."I know that's part of racing. I know that can be part of sport, but it's also further damage from the cars that we had the last few years."And now if we continue with finding this acceptable to drive on, then you are going to suffer with that much more."World champion Lando Norris backed Verstappen's opinion, saying: "The regulation of building a new track, the tolerances you have to be within are pretty small. It certainly doesn't fit anywhere close to what those regulations are now."It's an old track, not a new track so it's pretty bad. There's a lot of places I need to take headache tablets before I go out simply because it's so bumpy and you're hitting your head pretty hard against the headrest and things because of the bumps so it's certainly not a nice thing. There's not much we can do. I mean we complain about it so it's stuff we've brought up many, many times but there's only so much we can complain about things. But he's right."But Mercedes driver George Russell said: "It's bumpy, but I think it's just part of racing. I'd say my general view is F1 tracks probably need to be repaved every couple of years just to make it a bit more consistent. Because we're going to tracks now where Tarmac's coming up, it's falling apart, it's causing more issues than not."Not ideal, but not much we can do."

schema.headline: United States Grand Prix: Max Verstappen says Austin track bumps 'unacceptable' and 'out of control'

title: Caroline Flack's brother never recovered, inquest hears
description: The brother of TV presenter Caroline Flack took his own life having "never recovered" after his sister's death, an inquest heard.Paul Flack, 55, was f
body: The brother of TV presenter Caroline Flack took his own life having "never recovered" after his sister's death, an inquest heard.Paul Flack, 55, was found unresponsive at his home in Sandringham Road, Norwich, on 21 June, and died later in hospital.His partner told Norfolk Coroner's Court how he had struggled with his father developing dementia and his younger sister's death in 2020.Area Coroner Johanna Thompson gave a narrative conclusion, stating Paul Flack died while under the influence of alcohol and that his "intent in doing so is unknown".He was described as "everyone's favourite person" by his partner Joanna Millington, but she said this "took its toll".His sister, the ex-Love Island and X Factor host, was found dead at her home in Stoke Newington, east London, on 15 February 2020."We then went into lockdown for Covid," said Millington, who provided a written statement to the court."I do not think Paul ever recovered from this."An inquest later established Caroline Flack took her own life, aged 40, having feared press intrusion ahead of her trial accused of assaulting her boyfriend.

title: Dream night for Bournemouth - how did the Premier League come to dominate Europe?
description: At times, being a Bournemouth fan must feel like living in a simulation.That was certainly the case on Thursday night as the Cherries beat seven-time
body: At times, being a Bournemouth fan must feel like living in a simulation.That was certainly the case on Thursday night as the Cherries beat seven-time continental champions AC Milan 3-0 in only their third-ever European fixture.Justin Kluivert scored the opener at Vitality Stadium, 31 years after his father, Patrick, scored the winning goal for Ajax against Milan in the Champions League final.Having seen their club narrowly avoid the jaws of liquidation in 2008, not many Bournemouth fans would have dreamed that famous name would one day appear on their shirts."It's mega. In terms of the story of the club it's ridiculous. Someone told me today, 15 years ago today we were 17th in League One, so it's pretty incredible," Bournemouth midfielder Ryan Christie told TNT Sports."So many of these fans have been here for this journey so to have nights like this and win as well is special."To add to the peculiarity of the situation, Milan fielded more English players in their starting XI (three) than the hosts (two).While the sending off of Milan goalkeeper Mike Maignan killed the contest after 27 minutes, Bournemouth were by far the better side up until that point.In truth, that didn't come as a surprise, even though Bournemouth have won just six points from seven league games this term while Milan are fourth in Serie A.The three sides they have beaten this season - Real Sociedad, Sturm Graz, and now Milan - have all competed in the Champions League inside the past three years.For them it's a fairytale, but for the rest of Europe, is it a Premier League-induced nightmare?Five months after a missed Arsenal penalty denied a Premier League clean sweep in the Champions League, Europa League and Conference League, is this yet another sign of English club dominance?English clubs played nine games in Europe this week, losing just once.In fact, Premier League clubs have lost just four of 26 games played across the three continental competitions so far this season. Manchester United are responsible for two of them.In the five seasons since the Conference League was introduced, no league has yet won all three, but in three different seasons Premier League clubs have won two of them.Over the past two seasons, Premier League clubs have played 21 knockout ties against European opposition in the Conference League and Europa League - and won all 21.The only two ties they have lost have been to other English teams.But, despite such dominance, the Champions League still remains elusive for most, with only Manchester City lifting the trophy over the past five years.So, why are English clubs so dominant in Europe's secondary competitions - and why hasn't this transferred to consistent Champions League glory?Fifteen of last season's 20 Premier League teams featured in the top 30 of Deloitte's 2026 Money List.It is easy to see why then English clubs appear to be head and shoulders above the rest when it comes to the Europa League and the Conference League.Premier League clubs earn more than £1.37bn per season in television rights, a figure La Liga, Serie A, Bundesliga and Ligue 1 could only match combined.Brighton are easily the richest club in the Conference League this season, while Bournemouth and Crystal Palace both appear in last season's top 30.Last season Aston Villa beat Freiburg comfortably in the Europa League final, with a revenue more than double the Germans'.Crystal Palace won the Conference League with a revenue of almost four times more than Rayo Vallecano, the side they saw off in the final.In 2025, Tottenham beat Manchester United in the Europa League final. In the Premier League, they finished 17th and 15th respectively.In 2022-23, West Ham finished 14th and won the Conference League.All the evidence points to the Premier League's collective strength. Take away Europe's richest and England dominates.The summer transfer window was further evidence of Europe's struggles against the Premier League, with the latter again setting a new transfer spend record of £3.49bn to dwarf their rival leagues.Of the 20 most expensive transfers completed in the summer only six were not to clubs in the English top flight.You now have Premier League clubs - away from the traditional big six - beating other top European sides to signings.Premier League wages are generally higher and the league is increasingly seen as the place to be for a lot of European talent."With the exception of some of the global brands within football, and I think you'd look at Real Madrid, Barcelona, PSG and Bayern Munich, the Premier League can outspend anyone and everyone," football finance expert Kieran Maguire said in August."A significant proportion of overseas players are now choosing to play in England than elsewhere in Europe because of the wages on offer."Despite the success of Premier League sides in the Europa League and Conference League, the Champions League is a harder nut to crack.While Barcelona, Real Madrid and Bayern Munich all lost to English teams in last season's elongated Champions League league stage, it has been a very different story when it really mattered.Over the past two campaigns, eight of nine English teams have been knocked out by one of the Deloitte Money League's big four, according to the last report produced in January 2026.Chelsea, Manchester City, Newcastle and Liverpool were eliminated by an aggregate score of 25-6 last season.No English club appeared in the top four of Deloitte's Money List, with Real Madrid, Barcelona, Bayern Munich and Paris St-Germain leading the way. Three of those have won the Champions League five times between them in the last seven years.English clubs are certainly very much in the mix for the Champions League, with Arsenal losing last season's final on penalties and Manchester City winning in 2023.But, with just one English club in the past three finals, the Premier League elite are yet to take their European domination to the very top.Come May, it could well be Bournemouth, Brighton, Crystal Palace or Sunderland leading the English charge in Europe.

schema.headline: Dream night for Bournemouth - how did the Premier League come to dominate Europe?

title: Harry Brook underlines status as world's best all-format batter in Rawalpindi run-fest
description: In the moment, the collection of another landmark might not mean a great deal to Brook. Despite his efforts, his team were beaten as the spirited Sri
body: In the moment, the collection of another landmark might not mean a great deal to Brook. Despite his efforts, his team were beaten as the spirited Sri Lankans pulled off the second-highest run-chase in history in one of the most astonishing ODIs ever played.For a man who has previously spoken about prioritising match-winning contributions over individual achievements, Brook the captain was left dejected that his innings ultimately counted for nothing. He is the first man to make a double ton in an ODI and end up on the losing side.Still, it further underlined his status as the premier run-getter across all kinds of international cricket. Perhaps only Australia's Travis Head can challenge Brook for the crown.Ranked by the International Cricket Council as the best Test batter in the world, Brook averages 53.08 in the longer format of the game. No England player with a minimum of 20 innings since 1968 has a better average than Brook – he stands above Joe Root, Alastair Cook, Geoffrey Boycott, Graham Gooch and everyone else to have batted for England in the past seven decades.In T20 internationals, Brook averages 36.21 at a strike-rate of 164.92. No batter to have played at least 20 innings for a major nation averages more at a better strike-rate.Brook is learning to play List A cricket in one-day internationals. Sri Lanka was his 61st List A match, 45 of which have been ODIs. After a slow start to his international 50-over career, Brook averages just under 50 in his past 29 matches and almost 57 in 2026.The responsibility of captaincy suits him. In ODIs, Brook averages 31 runs more as captain compared to when not. In T20s, his average jumps 19 runs when wearing the metaphorical armband.Brook's workload is an issue, the Yorkshireman having played in every England fixture since being rested for a T20 series in Ireland last September and, fitness permitting, he will be the only man to play in every game this winter – that's five tours to four countries across three continents. He left home last week and will not again see his own bed until mid-January.He says his time to rest is during the Indian Premier League, the riches of which he has turned down in order to focus his energy on England. Brook probably does not get enough credit for making such a decision.There is the question of how good Brook could become. Ben Stokes revealed that, at the end of the Ashes, he took Brook to one side to say he should be averaging 60 or more in Test cricket.Speaking to the BBC in August, Brook admitted to not being the "finished article"."I have the ability to hit it everywhere, I just have to figure it out quicker in games," he said.In terms of improvement, Brook has already shown a willingness to do the hard yards to become a better cricketer.As a youngster, he struggled with his fitness, but has worked hard to become one of the best athletes in the England team. He has spoken at length about being better able to run twos – he is one of the best runners between the wickets in the world. Brook has also turned himself into one of England's most reliable catchers.As for the batting, well-qualified judges don't hold back in their praise. Last month, Stokes said Brook may have more talent than Kevin Pietersen. In 2024, James Anderson said Brook could surpass Root as England's highest Test run-scorer. Just last week, Chris Woakes labelled Brook as "next level".The missing achievement is a starring role in winning a major series or tournament.Brook's magnificent century should have been enough for England to win the fifth Test against India at The Oval last year, only for him to throw away his wicket with victory in sight. He has not made a century in 10 Ashes Tests against Australia and was only a bit-part player as part of the England team that won the T20 World Cup in 2022.Maybe his moment is approaching. Next summer is a home Ashes, followed by the 50-over World Cup in southern Africa. Brook will be 28 and at the peak of his powers. There is the chance to play a major part in regaining the urn and to become one of the few British athletes to lift a World Cup in any sport.To do that, he will have to iron out the flaws that have arisen in England's one-day cricket across the first two matches of the tri-series in Pakistan.In the opening match, against Pakistan, dropped catches and poor strokes left them well beaten in a contest they could have won.Against Sri Lanka, England somehow lost from what seemed an impregnable position, their bowling and fielding falling apart amid a growing realisation they were in danger of failing to defend a target of 430.There was some mitigation. Dew made the ball incredibly slippery, while their attack was weakened by the absence of the rested Jofra Archer and benched Adil Rashid.Nevertheless, the bowling was awful, particularly Sam Curran, who conceded 103 from nine overs to return the worst figures by an England bowler in an ODI. It was an error by Brook to continue to show faith in the left-armer, while not using the full allocation of 10 overs from either Josh Tongue or Gus Atkinson.It is one of the first major missteps of Brook's captaincy career and the sort of performance that shows England still have some way to go to be seen as serious World Cup contenders.Now, England will have to win their next two matches to reach the tri-series final, to be played on 31 October, exactly 12 months on from Brook's horror show in Wellington.England need the sort of turnaround their captain has managed over the past year

title: US actor Tom Skerritt, who starred in Top Gun, dies aged 93
description: US actor Tom Skerritt, who starred in Top Gun, Steel Magnolias and Alien, dies aged 93US actor Tom Skerritt, who starred in the TV series Picket Fence
body: US actor Tom Skerritt, who starred in Top Gun, Steel Magnolias and Alien, dies aged 93US actor Tom Skerritt, who starred in the TV series Picket Fences and the films Alien and Top Gun, has died aged 93, his family says. Skerritt died on Wednesday of natural causes, his family said: "While the world knew Tom through his remarkable acting career, we knew him for his humour, curiosity, wisdom, generosity, and the love he brought into our lives."In a six-decade career, he took on film and TV roles, appearing in the film Mash, A River Runs Through It and Ted. He also co-founded TheFilmSchool in Seattle to support next-generation filmmakers and storytellers.His family said he will be remembered "for his belief that stories can help people heal, find purpose, and create change".The moustachioed star of several 20th century hit films was born in 1933 in Detroit, Michigan, and served in the US Air Force before pursuing an acting career that boasted several military roles.He made his film debut in 1962 alongside a young Robert Redford ​in War Hunt and years later re-teamed with Redford in the 1992 period drama A River Runs Through It, which starred Brad Pitt. Skerritt's breakthrough role came when he played US army surgeon Duke Forrest in the 1970 Korean War comedy Mash, which also starred Donald Sutherland, Elliott Gould and Sally Kellerman. The hit film, which was released amid unrest over the Vietnam War, was nominated for five Academy Awards and was adapted for television two years later.He also starred alongside Sigourney Weaver in the 1979 sci-fi film Alien, which earned two Oscar nominations, and led to three sequels and several crossover projects."It is spontaneity and impulse ​that make the difference, and that is ⁠what I felt we had with 'Alien,'" Skerritt said in a 2019 interview, according to Reuters news agency."Every one of us had that immediate rapport with each other."Skerritt said that one of the things he liked most when he first read the script was that "the woman becomes a hero", referring to Weaver's character, Ripley.During his career, he starred opposite several strong female leads.He appeared with Shirley MacLaine in the 1977 film Turning Point and played Sally Field's husband in 1989's Steel Magnolias.As Commander Mike "Viper" Metcalf in the 1986 classic Top Gun, the versatile actor appeared alongside a young Tom Cruise in the blockbuster.On television, he won an Emmy Award in 1993 for his role as Sheriff Jimmy Brock in David E Kelley's drama Picket Fences. The quirky procedural's ensemble cast was nominated for SAG Awards in 1995 and 1996, and he received a nod for male actor in a drama series in 1995.Picket Fences star Lauren Holly, who played Skerritt's deputy on Picket Fences, described him in a tribute as "our leader"."His example made those years such a joy and we all loved and respected him so much," Holly wrote, adding: "He cared deeply for his family-both the one at home and the one at work. He cared deeply for his planet, and all of its inhabitants. He had a huge impact on my life, and so many memories I have of him include sharing fits of crippling laughter."Skerritt also had guest roles on the small screen in The West Wing, Madam Secretary, Law & Order: SVU and Huff. He reteamed with Field as the family patriarch, William Walker, in the drama Brothers & Sisters from 2007-09.He had a six-episode stint on Cheers playing Rebecca Howe's crush-worthy boss Evan Drake.In a statement, Skerritt's family said that he leaves behind a "legacy that reaches far beyond the screen". A deep believer in the power of storytelling, Skerritt helped found the TheFilmSchool in Seattle and co-founded the Red Badge Project, which helps veterans work through PTSD, anxiety and depression by writing and sharing their experiences.Inspired in part by his experience filming A River Runs Through It, he also believed in protecting the natural world. He created the documentary series Reflections of the River about America's rivers and supported river conservation.Skerrit is survived by his third wife Julie, five children and several grandchildren.

title: Dame Judi Dench: I can't do a play, do a film, or read any more
description: Dench also discussed meeting American actor Sidney Poitier, who became the first black man to win the Academy Award for best actor in 1964.She was app
body: Dench also discussed meeting American actor Sidney Poitier, who became the first black man to win the Academy Award for best actor in 1964.She was appearing in Amy's View in New York when Poitier came backstage after a performance. She recalled that director Richard Eyre was in her dressing room, giving her notes, when there was a knock at the door.Dench said she felt as if she were in a wind tunnel when Poitier walked in, adding: "It was thrilling."Asked what she had said to him, Dench replied: "Not much, a bit of an open mouth. So charming. Very tall."The conversation then turned to Dench's love of Shakespeare. She recalled watching her brother play King Duncan in Macbeth when she was nine and said the moment sparked her passion for the playwright."He walked on and he said 'What bloody man is that?' I thought, 'oh my God, this is for me'. He said 'bloody', did you hear that?"She also admitted to being " besotted" by Shakespeare's sonnets: "I just love them.""It's the rhythm of it. It's the rhythm of your heart," she added, "it's the way he's summed up so simply the way that any of us feel about, well, anything."

schema.headline: Dame Judi Dench: I can't do a play, do a film, or read any more
